 ORDER

The petitioners are before this Court calling in question the proceedings in C.C.No.5644/2020,
pending before the II Civil Judge & JMFC, Mysuru, for the offences under Sections 498A, 323, 504,
506 and 114 r/w. 34 of the IPC.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioners have filed a memo along with a joint affidavit of settlement and a copy of the order passed in MFA.No.6412/2021, disposed by a Division NC: 2023:KHC:20959 Bench of this Court on 16.01.2023, on the undertaken of the parties that they would settle the dispute among themselves and learned counsel for respondent No.2 would also accept the same.

3. The settlement recorded by the Division Bench insofar as it concerns the present lis reads as follows;
"3.

Apart from the above appeal, the parties have filed the following cases against each other, which are as follows:
a) C.C.No.590/2020 filled by the appellant for offences under Section 114, 504, 506,
324 r/w 34 of IPC which is pending adjudication before JMFC, II Court, Mysuru.

Judge Family Court, Mysuru in Crl.Misc.No.689/2019, granting a monthly maintenance of Rs.15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) to the respondent and the minor child.

f) Crl.P.No.8237/2021 filed by the appellant against the respondent pending before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru for quashing of the proceedings in C.C.No.5644/2020 filed against the appellant under Section 498-A, 323, 504, 506, 114, 34 of IPC r/w Sections 3 & 4 of D.P.
Act, which is pending adjudication.
4. In view of the parties prosecuting cases as aforementioned, they reached a point of no return and the marriage between them has broken irretrievably.
5. In view of the parties living separately from July 2017 and prosecuting the case against each other, they cannot continue to live as husband and wife any more.
Efforts made by elders and well-wishers on both sides have failed and accordingly the appellant and the respondent have decided to get an order of divorce.

6. Both the parties state they have obtained a loan jointly from Indian Overseas Bank, Bogadi Branch, Mysuru with account No.315903464000001 for development and putting up of construction on site bearing No.238, 3rd Cross, Roopanagar, Jayapura Hobli, Mysuru measuring 60x40 feet.
Out of the loan a sum of Rs.32,50,000/- (Rupees Thirty Two Lakhs Fifty Thousand Only) is pending and yet to be cleared.

7. The appellant has agreed to offer a sum of Rs.47,00,000/- (Rupees Forty Seven Lakhs Only) NC:
2023:KHC:20959 as full and final settlement to the respondent and the childof all their claims.

The respondent has agreed that out of the said amount of Rs.47,00,000/- (Rupees Forty Seven Lakhs Only), a sum of Rs.32,50,000/- (Rupees Thirty Two Lakhs Fifty Thousand Only) is to be paid to the Sri Naveen Kumar B vs State Of Karnataka on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151173756/
3 Bank by the appellant and the balance of Rs.14,50,000/- (Rupees Fourteen Lakhs Fifty Thousand Only) is to be paid by the appellant to the respondent for the maintenance and upbringing of the minor child.

sentences.text:
The appellant has already obtained a Banker's cheque for Rs.32,50,000/- (Rupees Thirty Two Lakhs Fifty Thousand Only) bearing No.025386 dated 12.12.2022 issued by HDFC Bank,
V.V. Mohalla Branch, Mysuru to be handed over to the Indian Overseas Bank and obtain a clearance certificate from the bank to be handed over to the appellant.
The appellant agrees not to make any claim against the respondent in respect of the house property.
The appellant has handed over the D.D. as aforementioned to the respondent today.

8. In the event of the respondent not coming forward for withdrawing/settling the cases as aforementioned, the amount of Rs.32,50,000/- (Rupees Thirty Two Lakhs Fifty Thousand Only)
paid vide Demand Draft shall be returned with interest within one month from the date of such act of denial.

9. The respondent states that she is gainfully employed with NIE, Mysuru and she does not have any claim against the appellant except the above amount either towards maintenance for past, present or future.

10. In view of the settlement entered into both parties agree that they will withdraw all the cases filed by them against each other and co-operate in getting the same cleared before the respective court.

The parties shall also provide consent/no objection before the Hon'ble courts for the NC:
2023:KHC:20959 petitions to be allowed/quashed and facilitate speedy disposal."
In the light of the statement recorded by the Division Bench as afore-extracted and the offence being the one punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 and 114 of the IPC and not against the State,
I deem
it appropriate to obliterate the proceedings against the petitioners

. 
4. For the aforestated reasons, the following:
ORDER a.
The criminal petition is disposed.
b. The proceedings in C.C.No.5644/2020, pending before the II Civil Judge and JMFC, Mysuru, stand quashed.
